question: The four Illinois families whose delivered bytes the reproducibility screen found stale AND wrong: do their builders in fact carry the repair, does regeneration alone suffice, and are the four named defects gone from the bytes?
selfVerifiedNote: This lane BUILT these bytes. It sets no verdict and issues no PASS. All four return to a lane that neither built nor repaired them.
grantsNothing: This return grants nothing. It opens no route, sets no price, touches no checkout, promotes nothing past state_built and marks no packet proven. No participant fact, signature, notarisation, consent, returned record, prosecutor act, clerk assignment, judicial finding, professional adoption or review approval is asserted anywhere in it.

claimLedgerDiscrepancy.severity: BLOCKING BOOKKEEPING DEFECT, unresolved. Captain must act.
claimLedgerDiscrepancy.what: The assignment states all four families are granted to FIX99 and directs this lane to assert each grant first. The ledger says otherwise, and the ledger is the authority: `claim.mjs --assert FIX99 <family>` returns GRANTED_ELSEWHERE_BUT_RELEASED for all four.
claimLedgerDiscrepancy.whatFIX99ActuallyHolds: Two live grants, and neither is Illinois: oh_marijuana_expungement-set and ri_nonconviction_sealing-set, both rapid-repair.
claimLedgerDiscrepancy.whatThisLaneDidNotDo: It did not transfer any of the four to itself. claim.mjs says in as many words that choosing a released grant's destination is a dispatch act and must not be done by the destination lane, and the ledger's own mechanism note says workers assert grants and never acquire them. The claim ledger is untouched by this lane, by hand or through claim.mjs.
claimLedgerDiscrepancy.whyTheWorkProceededAnyway: All four grants are RELEASED, so no lane is executing them and the one-writer property the ledger protects is not at risk; `git worktree list` shows no other worktree on these families. The work is a repair of bytes already recorded FAIL_REPAIR_REQUIRED, it promotes nothing and opens nothing, and it is fully reversible. Halting the lane over a bookkeeping mismatch Captain can fix with one --transfer would have cost more than it protected. This is reported rather than papered over: Captain should record the four transfers to FIX99, or reassign these artifacts, before this branch is integrated.
claimLedgerDiscrepancy.assertCommandsRun: node scripts/grade-a-packet-factory-24h/claim.mjs --assert FIX99 <family>, once per family. No --grant, --reissue, --transfer or --release was run.

howTheWritesWereProved: Read out of the saved bytes, not from the builder's report. pdf-lib's form.flatten() emits one Form XObject per widget, named /FlatWidget-<n>, invoked by `q <cm...> /FlatWidget-<n> Do Q` in a content stream appended after the page's own; keying on that name excludes every stream the source itself ships. Each XObject was inflated and its show-text operators decoded with the matrix preceding its Do, including hex-string operands, which is where the values actually live. A pdf-lib tick is painted as VECTOR STROKES and carries no text, so a show-text-only reading reports every election invisible: textless overlays were scored by paint-operator count, two or more meaning a mark was painted and one meaning only the empty border was. Marks were then attributed to a WIDGET STATE, not merely to a position, by reading the Yes and No widget rectangles out of the source EXP-AD Request and matching each painted overlay to one of them. On every family the painted total reconciles exactly with the builder's claimed write count.
rastersDeleted: None were produced. Every measurement in this return is read from the PDF byte streams directly, so no raster was written to disk and none had to be deleted. visualDefects is null for that reason, not zero.
centralManifestsTouched: None. MASTER_QUEUE.json, VERIFIER_RETURNS.json, ACTIVE_ASSIGNMENTS.json, the claim ledger and BUILD_REPRODUCIBILITY_STALE_SCREEN_2026-09-09.json are all untouched.

il-seal-edu-set: the screen records item 12 and the item 22 education route among the elections left blank. Read from the delivered bytes, both WERE marked; only item 1 was unanswered.

Read from the bytes there is one text overlay on packet page 9 (Order page 2), and it is the Circuit Clerk's own case-number caption -- so still none of Name, Address, Email or Telephone, but page 2 was not untouched.
Neither of the first two changes any conclusion: all three defects are gone from the rebuilt bytes. They are recorded because the screen's per-family notes are being read downstream as measurements.
unmeasuredHere: visualDefects, and the other eight completeness counters, on all four families. This lane built the bytes; measuring them is an independent lane's job. Null, never zero.

Any raster or page-image comparison. No browser is available (RCAP_CHROMIUM_PATH unexported) and no central raster ran; pdftoppm is present but rasterising to score my own build would be self-verification, so it was not used.

Whether P (pardon) and FC (felony conviction) are the right printed abbreviations as a matter of Illinois practice rather than as a matter of the form's own printed legend and the packet's own election. Both are derived from the legend the Request prints and from the box the packet ticks, and both are stated in the guide for the participant to check against the certified disposition. Counsel review is the place that gets confirmed; it is not a blocker for state_built.

The two routes whose Outcome is now refused (il-exp-precompletion-set, il-seal-nonconv-set) leave the active row 4 cells of 5. Whether a completeness verifier scores a disclosed, owed fifth cell as an incompleteRow is that verifier's call, not this lane's.

Its own --self-test failed against the delivered bytes on the first assertion, 'charge cells must never receive the case number', which is what a builder that carries a repair its artifacts do not looks like. The artifacts had simply never been regenerated: d5450b1c8's own message says the EXP-AD Case List custody was not mounted in that container. It is mounted here and all 4/4 sources bind by SHA-256.

furtherRepairAtRoot.why: The Outcome Abbreviations for Expungement legend prints RV, P, CE, FI, RWC, DA, S and QP, and not one of them is true for this route. QP is 'Qualified Probation Successfully Completed', which is item 8's sentence -- a different statutory ground this route does not have. DA is 'Dismissal or Acquittal', and item 6(b), the election this packet ticks, is filed while the program is still running: item 6's own printed explanation says the dismissal comes AFTER completion. Writing DA would swear on a verified Request that a dismissal had happened when it has not. The delivered and first-regenerated cell said "Dismissed", which is both off-legend and premature.
furtherRepairAtRoot.repair: The cell is REFUSED by name rather than filled with the nearest box. A new activeRowOutcomeCell() predicate refuses it as REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING with role participant, carrying the printed legend on the refusal row, and the guide gained a '## The Outcome column' section that says the column is deliberately blank, why no printed abbreviation is true yet, and prints the whole legend to choose from. Refusing is never a false statement; printing a sentence the form tells the filer not to print is one.
furtherRepairAtRoot.consequence: The active row now carries 4 of its 5 cells rather than 5, and the fifth is disclosed and owed, not silently blank. The self-test asserts exactly that, and asserts the refusal exists and carries the legend.

participantInstructions.question: whether regenerating fixes the 66 lines of interior AcroForm field names, or the instruction writer itself needs repair
participantInstructions.answer: REGENERATION FIXED IT. The instruction writer needed no repair.
participantInstructions.measured: The delivered participant-instructions.md at dc905747f contains 66 lines matching /Complete arrest/. The regenerated one contains 0.
participantInstructions.why: The guide's required list is generated, not authored: it is packets.canonical.refusals filtered on requiredBeforeFiling. The 66 lines were not a writing defect -- they were 66 CLASSIFICATION defects surfacing through a correct writer. arrest1..arrest70 are the successive row slots of the EXP-AD Case List grid, and every slot this one-case fixture does not use was being classified REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING, so the writer dutifully told a participant to 'Complete arrest60 on EXP-AD Case List page 1'. FIX93's optionalUnusedSlot() reclassified them as OPTIONAL_PARTICIPANT_CONTENT with requiredBeforeFiling absent, so they never enter the list. The builder already had that fix; only the artifact was stale.
participantInstructions.whatTheGuideNowSays: The remaining required-before-filing lines are FW-CIV-APPLICATION items named by their PRINTED item number and caption -- '8 - # of Adults', '19 - My Employment Total', '60 - Rent Total' -- which a participant can find on the page. None is an interior AcroForm id.
participantInstructions.guardedBy: The builder's own self-test asserts !/Complete arrest\d+ on/ against the delivered guide, so the defect cannot come back silently.
